subject: matrix of vectors, row/column order in data file

messages.author: 275b133a3506805a
messages.subject: matrix of vectors, row/column order in data file
parts:
Hi all,

Just a little question - if I'm specifying some data as

vector[D] obs[M, N]; // feature data

then am I correct to expect that I should linearise my values in the
data file in the same order as a 3d array of shape [M, N, D], in
last-index-major form? (Just to spell it out, this means that if D=2,
then my vector at [m=0,n=0] has its two values actually quite far
apart from each other in the linear format, since all the d=1 values
are written out then the d=2 values.)

The manual spells it out for a 3d array (sec 6.3) but isn't explicit
about storage of vector or row_vector.

Thanks
Dan

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] matrix of vectors, row/column order in data file
parts:
On 9/20/13 4:19 AM, Dan Stowell wrote:
> Hi all,
>
> Just a little question - if I'm specifying some data as
>
> vector[D] obs[M, N]; // feature data
>
> then am I correct to expect that I should linearise my values in the
> data file in the same order as a 3d array of shape [M, N, D], in
> last-index-major form?

Exactly. It's because obs is a two-dimensional array of
vectors. So you access the array dimensions first.

In the dump format, the data will look exactly the same as if
you had declared this:

real obs[M,N,D];

> (Just to spell it out, this means that if D=2,
> then my vector at [m=0,n=0] has its two values actually quite far
> apart from each other in the linear format, since all the d=1 values
> are written out then the d=2 values.)

You can always troubleshoot by declaring:

vector[2] obs[3,4];

and then trying both ways. The wrong-way 'round will give you an error.

> The manual spells it out for a 3d array (sec 6.3) but isn't explicit
> about storage of vector or row_vector.

It's already been requested that we spell that out more
clearly, so I'm about to add an example to the manual for
Stan 2.0.

- Bob
